chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Awn ibn Amra al-Ansi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated from Malik ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Two characteristics do not coexist in a Muslim: stinginess and bad character.

key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: A Muslim (one who submits to God)

ai.seo_question: What two characteristics cannot coexist in a Muslim according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith emphasizes that true faith requires the harmonious integration of generosity and moral conduct, as stinginess and bad character are mutually exclusive with the essence of a Muslim. This pairing reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *akhlaq* (character) as the outward manifestation of inner *iman* (faith), where material detachment complements social grace. The Prophet’s silence in other instances further underscores the weight of these traits in defining spiritual integrity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-117 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Ibn Sa’ed quoted Al-Ab’bas ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Oan ibn Am’marat al-Etri, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Suleiman, on the authority of Malik ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Qalib, on the authority of Abi Sa’id al-Khidry that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“There are two characteristics which cannot co-exist in a Muslim: stinginess and being bad-tempered.”
